items.stem: A VR app causes nausea in many users after a few minutes. Which factor is the most likely primary cause to investigate first?

options.text: High motion-to-photon latency and mismatch between visual motion and the body's sense of motion
options.rationale: Correct: latency and sensory conflict are leading causes of VR motion sickness.

options.text: The headset's colour palette being too warm
options.rationale: Colour warmth is not a primary driver of motion sickness.

options.text: Using hand tracking instead of controllers
options.rationale: Input method is not the primary cause of nausea here.

options.text: The app icon being low resolution
options.rationale: The icon has no bearing on in-experience comfort.

items.explanation: Correct: latency and sensory conflict are leading causes of VR motion sickness.

items.stem: Which TWO statements correctly distinguish AR from VR? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AR overlays digital content onto the user's view of the real world
options.rationale: Correct: AR augments the real environment with digital content.

options.text: VR replaces the user's view with a fully synthetic environment
options.rationale: Correct: VR immerses the user in an entirely virtual scene.

options.text: AR always fully blocks out the real world
options.rationale: Blocking out the real world describes VR, not AR.

options.text: VR requires no display at all
options.rationale: VR depends on a display to present the virtual environment.

items.explanation: Correct: AR augments the real environment with digital content.

items.stem: Why is eye-tracking data in XR a particular privacy concern?

options.text: It can reveal sensitive information such as attention, intent and even health signals
options.rationale: Correct: gaze data is highly revealing and demands careful privacy handling.
The concern is privacy of the data, not rendering speed.

options.text: Because it is impossible to store
options.rationale: It can be stored; that is partly why it is sensitive.

options.text: Because eye tracking only works outdoors
options.rationale: This is false and unrelated to the privacy concern.

items.explanation: Correct: gaze data is highly revealing and demands careful privacy handling.
